school.hint.0.0: Mr Hollis left something on your desk.
school.hint.0.1: Turn to the timetable wall and look at your desk.
school.hint.0.2: Tap the envelope on your desk.
school.hint.1.0: Riddle 1: what is full of lights at night, but isn’t a city?
school.hint.1.1: The night sky! Find a book about it in the library.
school.hint.1.2: Go through the corridor to the library. Open The Night Sky on the blue Science shelf.
school.hint.2.0: The note says the key is in Mr Hollis’s art apron.
school.hint.2.1: The art room is off the corridor. Which apron has the paint on it?
school.hint.2.2: In the art room, tap the splattered apron by the sink, then take the key from its pocket.
school.hint.3.0: A key with a star. Where have you seen a star on a lock?
school.hint.3.1: The STEM cabinet in the hall has a star on its padlock.
school.hint.3.2: In the hall, tap the star key in the strip, then tap the cabinet’s padlock.
school.hint.4.0: The padlock is off. What did Mr Hollis leave in the STEM cabinet?
school.hint.4.1: Look inside the cabinet in the hall.
school.hint.4.2: Tap the STEM cabinet and take the slip from the shelf.
school.hint.5.0: Riddle 2: eighty-eight keys, and no doors. What could it be?
school.hint.5.1: A piano! But the Music shelf has a gap. Where do returned books go?
school.hint.5.2: In the library, find the returns trolley next to the Art shelf. Open Playing the Piano.
school.hint.6.0: Four coloured notes. Something in the school has four colours you can play.
school.hint.6.1: The chime bars on the hall stage. But what do you hit them with?
school.hint.6.2: In the hall’s playground corner, tap the stack of soft blocks. Something is under them.
school.hint.7.0: You have a beater. What does it play?
school.hint.7.1: Take the beater to the chime bars on the hall stage.
school.hint.7.2: Tap the beater in the strip, then tap the chime bars.
school.hint.8.0: Play the four notes from the page, in the order they are written.
school.hint.8.1: The colours on the page are the bars. Green first.
school.hint.8.2: Tap the bars green, red, blue, then yellow.
school.hint.9.1: A little drawer in the front of the stage has slid open.
school.hint.9.2: Tap the open drawer in the front of the stage.
school.hint.10.0: Riddle 3: full of colour, and brushes are its best friends.
school.hint.10.1: It’s a book about painting. Try the orange Art shelf in the library.
school.hint.10.2: Open The Big Book of Painting on the Art shelf.
school.hint.11.0: The note says Mr Hollis’s moth knows the colours.
school.hint.11.1: Mary’s moth painting is on the drying rack in the art room. Look under it.
school.hint.11.2: The three stripes under the moth are the padlock’s colours: purple, green, orange. Set the dials on the paint cupboard and tap Open.
school.hint.12.1: Look inside the paint cupboard in the art room.
school.hint.12.2: Tap the paint cupboard and take the slip from the shelf.
school.hint.13.0: You have three lessons and three days. The class timetable turns each into a number.
school.hint.13.1: The whiteboard says which picture is which lesson. Find each lesson on its day: the period number at the top is one number of your locker code.
school.hint.13.2: Science Thursday is 4, Music Tuesday is 3, Art Wednesday is 6. Set your locker in the corridor to 4, 3, 6.
school.hint.14.0: Your locker is open. What did Mr Hollis leave inside?
school.hint.14.1: Look inside your locker in the corridor.
school.hint.14.2: Tap the report and the postcard in your open locker.
school.note.envelope: For Mary It’s our last-day treasure hunt! Three riddles lead to three library books. Each book starts a trail, and at the end of each trail is a slip with a lesson and a day. Look each one up on our timetable: its period number is one number of your locker code, in riddle order. 1. At night I’m full of lights, but I’m not a city. 2. I have eighty-eight keys, but I can’t open a single door. 3. I’m full of colour, but I’m not a rainbow. Brushes are my best friends. Mr Hollis
school.note.noteStar: Found me! The key to the stars is in my art apron, the one with all the paint on it. Then look for the star. Mr H
school.note.notePaint: Found me! Your slip is locked in the paint cupboard. My moth knows the colours: look under it on the drying rack. Mr H
school.note.music: Playing the Piano, page 12: Holiday Song Four notes. Play me in the hall!
school.note.slipSc: Slip for riddle 1 SCIENCE on THURSDAY Find it on the timetable. Its period number is the first number of your locker code.
school.note.slipMu: Slip for riddle 2 MUSIC on TUESDAY Find it on the timetable. Its period number is the second number of your locker code.
school.note.slipAr: Slip for riddle 3 ART on WEDNESDAY Find it on the timetable. Its period number is the third number of your locker code.
school.note.bonus: Bonus riddle for super-sleuths Someone in London loves postcards and moths. Spell her name with the first letters of four stories.
school.card: Everyone is at the goodbye party in the hall. Tomorrow the whole family flies to London, to Nana and Jedi’s. But Mr Hollis has left something on Mary’s desk.
school.meanwhile: Meanwhile, at Knightsbrook, Mary is still hunting for the words in Mr Hollis’s riddle.
school.intro: Last day of school. Everyone is at the party, but Mr Hollis left something on your desk. And a little moth is watching from the window.
school.postcard: Last day! Mr Hollis set a treasure hunt with three riddles. I found a star key in his apron, played a tune on the chime bars, and cracked the paint cupboard. My report says “a brilliant detective”, and there was a postcard from Nana in my locker: “Not long now!” The little moth on it seems to glow.
packing.hint.0.0: Mum stuck a list up for you.
packing.hint.0.1: It’s on the wall by your bedroom door.
packing.hint.0.2: Tap the list beside your door.
packing.hint.1.0: What did Nana ask you to bring? Her postcard says.
packing.hint.1.1: Nana’s postcard is on the fridge in the kitchen.
packing.hint.1.2: Go to the kitchen and tap the postcard on the fridge.
packing.hint.2.0: The torch lives in the hall drawer by the front door.
packing.hint.2.1: Open the hall drawer in the living room. Something is in it, but not the torch.
packing.hint.2.2: Tap the hall drawer by the front door and read Elliot’s note.
packing.hint.3.0: Elliot says the password is on the fridge.
packing.hint.3.1: His crayon drawing on the fridge shows his base, and three symbols on its door.
packing.hint.3.2: Tap Elliot’s drawing on the fridge: sun, star, moon.
packing.hint.4.0: The password goes on the fort under the dining table.
packing.hint.4.1: Tap the blanket fort. Press the three symbols from Elliot’s drawing, in that order, then Knock.
packing.hint.4.2: On the fort: sun, star, moon, then Knock.
packing.hint.5.0: The fort is open. Elliot’s things are inside.
packing.hint.5.1: Tap the fort to look inside.
packing.hint.5.2: Take the torch from the cushion inside the fort.
packing.hint.6.0: Passports are kept somewhere safe. Somewhere with a lock.
packing.hint.6.1: Dad’s desk drawer has a keyhole. The keys hang on hooks beside the window.
packing.hint.6.2: Tap the hooks by the living-room window and take the key whose tag says DESK.
packing.hint.7.0: You have the desk key. Try it in the drawer.
packing.hint.7.1: Tap the desk key in the strip, then Dad’s desk drawer.
packing.hint.7.2: Use the key on the drawer, then take hold of the handle and pull.
packing.hint.8.0: The drawer is stuck. Someone in this flat will know the trick.
packing.hint.8.1: Ask Mum. She is in the kitchen.
packing.hint.9.0: Mum said: lift it up a little while you pull.
packing.hint.9.1: Back at Dad’s desk drawer: drag the front up a little, and keep hold.
packing.hint.9.2: Tap the drawer, drag the front up a finger’s width, then, still holding, drag it down and out.
packing.hint.10.0: What would Nana like? Her postcard might say.
packing.hint.10.1: Nana’s postcard is on the fridge in the kitchen.
packing.hint.10.2: Tap the postcard on the fridge and read the P.S.
packing.hint.11.0: Nana has run out of kaya.
packing.hint.11.1: Kaya is a jam. Where are the jars kept?
packing.hint.11.2: Tap the cupboard by the kitchen sink and take the kaya.
packing.hint.12.1: There is a roll of moth paper on Dad’s desk.
packing.hint.12.2: Take the paper from Dad’s desk, then tap the paper in the strip and tap the kaya.
packing.hint.13.0: The paper springs open. It needs tape.
packing.hint.13.1: Your pencil case on your desk has sticky tape in it.
packing.hint.13.2: Take the tape from your pencil case, tap it in the strip, then tap the half-wrapped present.
packing.hint.14.0: Everything on the list goes in the suitcase.
packing.hint.14.1: The suitcase is open on your bed.
packing.hint.14.2: Tap each thing in the strip, then tap the suitcase.
packing.hint.15.0: Everything is in. Now the suitcase has to be shut.
packing.hint.15.1: Tap the suitcase, then pull the zip across with your finger.
packing.hint.15.2: Tap the suitcase, take hold of the zip pull and drag it all the way round to the right corner.
packing.note.list: Mary, before the taxi at four: 1. The torch 2. The passports 3. Nana’s present And wear something warm on the plane! Mum x
packing.note.postcard: From Nana Dear Mary, not long now! Bring the little torch, you’ll need it. Jedi says hello (he is resting his eyes). Love, Nana x P.S. I’ve run out of kaya.
packing.note.ehnote: In Elliot’s crayon: BORROWED THE TORCH FOR MY BASE. PASSWORD ON THE FRIDGE. E
packing.card: Rain on the windows and the taxi at four. Mum has stuck a list on Mary’s bedroom door: three things that must not be forgotten.
packing.meanwhile: Meanwhile, at home, the taxi is at four and Mary’s suitcase is still open on the bed.
packing.intro: Packing day. Rain outside, the taxi at four, and a list from Mum on the wall by your door.
packing.postcard: Packed! The torch was in Elliot’s secret base (password: sun, star, moon), the passports were in Dad’s stuck drawer (Mum knew the trick), and I wrapped a jar of kaya for Nana in the moth paper. Fourteen hours to London. Elliot has his dinosaur, Zaina has Peanut, and I have my jumper on top.
eschool.hint.0.0: Miss Okafor left a card on her desk.
eschool.hint.0.1: The card is on the teacher’s desk, under the whiteboard.
eschool.hint.0.2: Tap the card on Miss Okafor’s desk.
eschool.hint.1.0: Three pieces are missing from the marble run. Which goes where?
eschool.hint.1.1: The class drew the finished run on the chalk wall in the playground.
eschool.hint.1.2: Go outside and tap the chalk wall: straight at the top, curve in the middle, zigzag at the bottom.
eschool.hint.2.0: One piece is right under the run.
eschool.hint.2.1: Look in the tray under the marble run.
eschool.hint.2.2: Tap the tray under the run and take the straight piece.
eschool.hint.3.1: Something bright is sticking out of the sandpit.
eschool.hint.3.2: Tap the sandpit in the playground and take the curved piece.
eschool.hint.4.0: One piece is somewhere warm and woolly.
eschool.hint.4.1: The lost-property box is on the bench outside. It is full of jumpers.
eschool.hint.4.2: Take your jumper out of the lost-property box: the zigzag piece is underneath.
eschool.hint.5.0: Hold a piece, then tap the marble run.
eschool.hint.5.1: The chalk drawing shows the order: straight, curve, zigzag, top to bottom.
eschool.hint.5.2: Tap a piece in the strip, tap the run, then tap the gap it belongs in.
eschool.hint.6.0: All three pieces are in. Now roll!
eschool.hint.6.1: Tap the marble run and press Roll.
eschool.hint.6.2: Tap the run, then Roll. The marble does the rest.
eschool.hint.7.0: Which jumper is yours? Your peg knows.
eschool.hint.7.1: Every peg has a name card with a little drawing. Find Elliot’s.
eschool.hint.7.2: Tap the coat pegs by the doorway and look at Elliot’s card.
eschool.hint.8.0: Your jumper is in lost property, with three others.
eschool.hint.8.1: The lost-property box is on the bench outside. Yours has the same picture as your peg card.
eschool.hint.8.2: Tap the box on the bench and take the jumper with the rocket badge.
eschool.hint.9.0: Bell rung, jumper found. Time for the card.
eschool.hint.9.1: Miss Okafor’s card is on her desk in the classroom.
eschool.hint.9.2: Tap the card on Miss Okafor’s desk.
eschool.note.card: On the front, in Miss Okafor’s writing: Goodbye, Elliot! Open me after the marble run works. And not without your jumper! Love from everyone in 2P
eschool.note.cardOpen: Inside the card, twenty-nine names, and: Have the best summer, Elliot. Keep asking how things work. Miss O x And in the corner, in someone’s pencil: a little moth.
eschool.card: Classroom 2P, with balloons on the whiteboard and a party waiting. Miss Okafor has left Elliot a card on her desk, and the marble run on the wall has never once rung its bell.
eschool.meanwhile: Meanwhile, in Classroom 2P, Elliot has a marble run to mend before anyone touches the cake.
eschool.intro: Last day of term. Balloons on the whiteboard, cake on the table, and a card with your name on it on Miss Okafor’s desk.
eschool.postcard: The marble run was missing three pieces: one in the tray, one in the sandpit and one under the jumpers in lost property. The chalk wall showed where they went, and when I pressed Roll the marble went ALL the way and rang the bell. I found my jumper too (rocket badge). Miss Okafor’s card has everybody’s name in it and someone drew a moth. See you at the airport!
zschool.hint.0.0: Your bottle is on the shelf. Find the yellow star!
zschool.hint.1.0: Put it in your cubby: the one with the yellow star.
zschool.hint.2.0: Your painting is on the line. Which one has the star?
zschool.hint.3.0: Pop it in your cubby, with the star.
zschool.hint.4.0: Play the goodbye song! Drum, shaker, bell, xylophone.
zschool.hint.5.0: All done! Go and see Miss Lin.
zschool.card: Little Waves Kindergarten, with flags across the ceiling and a cake on the table. Zaina’s mark is a yellow star. Her bottle, her painting and the goodbye song, then Miss Lin has something shiny.
zschool.meanwhile: Meanwhile, at Little Waves, Zaina’s party is about to start.
zschool.intro: Party day! Find your bottle and your painting, they have your yellow star. Then the goodbye song, then Miss Lin.
zschool.line.cubbies: Everyone has a cubby. Yours has the yellow star.
zschool.line.cubbyMine: Your cubby! The yellow star. Your bottle and your painting go in here.
zschool.line.cubbyOther: Not that one. Look for the yellow star.
zschool.line.cubbyFull: Your bottle and your painting, safe in your cubby.
zschool.line.shelf: The bottles are up on the shelf. Which one is yours?
zschool.line.shelfEmpty: Only the other children’s bottles now.
zschool.line.bottleWrong: Not that one. Yours has the yellow star.
zschool.line.bottleMine: The yellow star! That’s your bottle. Now put it in your cubby.
zschool.line.line: Paintings on the line. Which one is yours?
zschool.line.lineEmpty: Only the other children’s paintings now.
zschool.line.paintingWrong: Not that one. Yours has the yellow star in the corner.
zschool.line.paintingMine: The star! That’s your painting: the sun and the elephant. Now put it in your cubby.
zschool.line.paints: Red, blue and yellow. All the colours you need.
zschool.line.window: Sunshine outside. Mummy is coming soon.
zschool.line.poster: The goodbye song! Drum, shaker, bell, xylophone. Play them in that order.
zschool.line.shelf3: Drum, shaker, bell, xylophone. Look at the poster and play them in order.
zschool.line.songNotYet: Not that one yet. Look at the poster.
zschool.line.songDone: That’s the goodbye song! Everyone claps.
zschool.line.songAgain: You played the goodbye song. Lovely.
zschool.line.rug: The story rug. No story today, it’s party day.
zschool.line.table: The party table. Cake for later.
zschool.line.cake: The cake! Three candles. Not yet.
zschool.line.fruit: Apples, an orange and a banana.
zschool.line.misslinWait: Miss Lin is busy with the party. Bottle, painting and the song first.
zschool.line.misslinDone: Miss Lin turns round. “Zaina! All done? Then this is for you.”
zschool.line.sticker: A shiny moth sticker! For being a star.
zschool.line.putBottle: In it goes. Your bottle, in your cubby.
zschool.line.putPainting: In it goes. Your painting, in your cubby.
zschool.line.wrongPlace: Not there. It goes in your cubby, with the star.
zschool.postcard: I found my bottle and my painting (they have my STAR on) and put them in my cubby, and I played the goodbye song on the drum and the shaker and the bell and the xylophone, and Miss Lin gave me a moth sticker. Peanut helped. (Miss Lin wrote this down for me.)
howto: Tap anything you are curious about. The little arrows turn you round. Things you pick up wait in the strip: tap one, then tap where it goes. And if you are stuck, tap me.
tip.tap: Tap anything you are curious about. The little arrows at the sides turn you round.
tip.pickup: Things you pick up wait in the strip below. Tap one to hold it, then tap where it belongs.
tip.hold: Now tap the thing it goes with. Tap it in the strip again to put it down.
tip.combine: Two things in the strip can go together: hold one, then tap the other.
tip.help: If you get stuck, tap me at the top: your notebook has a hint for every riddle. And hold a finger on the room to see everything you can tap.
tip.helpPoint: If you get stuck, tap me at the top and I’ll fly to the next thing to look at.
